title: Indian-American Hanu Karlapalem Wins National STEM Endorsement for Alabama House Race
excerpt: The technology entrepreneur and naturalized U.S. citizen is challenging a two-term Republican incumbent in North Alabama while fighting a state bill that would bar immigrants from public office.
body:
• Hanu Karlapalem, an Indian-American technology entrepreneur, has received a national STEM endorsement from the 314 Action Fund in his race for Alabama State House District 4.
  • Karlapalem, a naturalized U.S. citizen who emigrated from India 26 years ago, is the Democratic nominee challenging Republican incumbent Parker Moore in the November 3 general election.
  • His campaign centres on three pillars — Economy First, People First, Constitution First — with focus on lowering costs, strengthening public schools, and expanding healthcare access.
  • Karlapalem has been a vocal opponent of Alabama Senate Bill 21, which would bar naturalized citizens from holding public office in the state.

From India to Alabama’s Ballot

Hanu Karlapalem, a technology entrepreneur who moved from India to Alabama more than two decades ago, has received a national endorsement from the 314 Action Fund, a political organization that supports candidates with backgrounds in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The endorsement adds national visibility to Karlapalem’s bid for Alabama State House District 4, where he is the Democratic nominee facing two-term Republican incumbent Parker Moore in the November 3, 2026 general election.

The 314 Action Fund, which has endorsed 241 candidates across 25 states for the 2026 cycle, backs Democratic candidates who bring scientific and technical expertise to public office. Karlapalem, founder and CEO of Vinhamz Inc., a Madison-based consulting firm specializing in network and cloud services, fits that profile — he holds a Master of Science in Management Information Systems from the University of Alabama in Huntsville and has more than three decades of experience in business, engineering, and information technology.

A Platform Built on Affordability

Karlapalem’s campaign is organized around three governing principles: Economy First, People First, and Constitution First. His core policy priorities include lowering costs for Alabama families, strengthening public school funding, and expanding healthcare access in District 4, which covers portions of Morgan, Limestone, and Madison counties in North Alabama’s high-tech corridor.

“While Alabama families are tightening their belts, the supermajority legislature and special interests are tightening their grip. This campaign is about an Alabama we can afford.”

— Hanu Karlapalem, Democratic Nominee, Alabama House District 4

He has been particularly vocal on education policy, criticizing the state’s CHOOSE Act as a mechanism to redirect public school funding to private institutions. Karlapalem estimates districts in House District 4 could lose approximately $100 million annually under the programme. He has also taken positions on housing affordability, calling for mandatory sex offender registry screening for short-term rental platforms and legislation restricting corporate investors from purchasing single-family homes.

Fighting SB21: The Anti-Naturalized Citizen Bill

Karlapalem’s candidacy has been shaped by Alabama Senate Bill 21, a proposed constitutional amendment that would bar naturalized U.S. citizens from holding public office in the state. Sponsored by State Senator Donnie Chesteen and championed by Secretary of State Wes Allen, the bill would affect positions including state legislator, mayor, city council member, and sheriff.

Karlapalem has led opposition to the bill, gathering more than 1,250 petition signatures and sending formal objections to Governor Kay Ivey and state lawmakers. “SB21 is unconstitutional, un-American, and dangerous,” Karlapalem told ALPolitics.com. “If you are born or naturalized in the United States, you are a citizen — full, equal, and indivisible. The Fourteenth Amendment does not have an asterisk.”

Roots in Community Service

A 26-year resident of Madison, Alabama, Karlapalem has built an extensive civic record. He is a Life Member and former Second Vice President of the Limestone County NAACP, served as chairman of the AANHPI Caucus within the Alabama Democratic Party, and sat on the State Democratic Executive Committee and the UAH Alumni Association board. He previously ran for Madison mayor in 2016 and the Limestone County Commission in 2018. In 2024, he received the Spirit of Diplomacy Award for international engagement efforts.

His wife, Vidya Karlapalem, holds a master’s degree in computer science and works as a Senior Software Engineer for a global company in Huntsville. The couple has been married for 31 years.

Indian-Americans in the Political Arena

Karlapalem’s candidacy reflects the growing political engagement of Indian-Americans across the United States. While Indian-Americans have reached prominent positions in national politics, representation at the state and local level remains thin, particularly in Southern states. A victory in District 4 — a reliably Republican seat that has never seen a serious challenge — would be historic. The general election is scheduled for November 3, 2026.
